newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan says considering buying Argentine wheat.
newsitem.headline: Japan says considering buying Argentine wheat.

text.p: Japan is considering importing wheat from Argentina for the first time in 22 years, in an attempt to diversify its source of suppliers, a Food Agency official said on Friday.

Japan's main suppliers now are the United States, Canada and Australia. "Argentina recently approached us and asked if Japan was interested in buying Argentine wheat," the Food Agency's trade division director Shinichi Yahagi told Reuters.
"We're going to receive some samples of Argentine wheat soon. And if local end-users are satisfied with the quality, we'll buy," Yahagi said.
But he did not say when and in what amounts Japan might buy.
The Food Agency, the grain trading arm of the Agriculture Ministry, is Japan's sole importer of wheat, barley and rice.
